title: Structures and members
goal: Group a sensor identifier and its reading in one record, update a working copy safely, and retain the original reading.

prerequisites.text: Read integer assignment and distinguish numbers from text.
Know how to check a range before applying a calculation. The starter supplies input parsing.

terms.title: Record
terms.definition: A group of fields describing one object or event.

terms.title: Member
terms.definition: A named part of a structure. For example, the reading has id and millivolts members.

terms.title: Structure copy
terms.definition: Assignment between structures of the same type copies their member values. Both members in this example are integers.

sections.title: Fields belong to one measurement
paragraphs: The laboratory log pairs sensor number 14 with its reading of 320 mV. With separate variables, a copy operation might accidentally move only half of the record.
The declaration struct Sample defines a type. The object current gets its own member values. The dot operator selects a member of that object.
Designated initializers .id and .millivolts bind values to member names. C permits padding between members and at the end, so the structure's memory representation is not a file format.
Named fields distinguish the roles of the numbers. Copying a structure with a pointer member copies the pointer value. It does not duplicate the target object.

Draw two log rows with the same id and millivolts columns. With one row, an adjustment changes the only reading. Copying creates a second row from the current values of both fields. You can then correct the working row and still have the original reading to compare.

sections.title: Save a snapshot before applying a correction
paragraphs: Predict the third number. The log must show the sensor identifier, the corrected reading and the reading at the time of the snapshot.
Trace two moments: just after copying and just after the correction. In the first, the rows are identical. In the second, one field changes in the working row only. Name that field before running.
steps: Create current with identifier 14 and reading 320.
Copy the entire record to archived. The two objects now contain identical values.
Add 15 to current.millivolts. archived retains 320 because it already contains a separate copy of the integer members.

sections.title: Locate and check the defect
paragraphs: Clang reports no member named for the typo millivolt. Compare the name after the dot with the declaration of struct Sample. Correct only the member name and rebuild.
If both printed readings are 335, check the order of the copy and correction. The program can compile successfully even when the snapshot is taken at the wrong time.

sections.title: Change, predict and check
paragraphs: Change 15 to -20 in the example and write down the values of current and archived before running it. Then transfer the same order of operations to a different record with input bounds.
A pointer member would copy the pointer value itself. Here the record deliberately uses integer members only, so the two readings are independent.

reading.purpose: Review the language constructs used in the worked example.

feedback: The earlier snapshot retains the original value.
The third number belongs to the separate object archived.
The current reading is printed before the snapshot.

selfcheck.prompt: Where should the corrected value be checked?
feedback: Check the result before storing it.
By then the invalid state has already been used.
Both the input and the operation's result need validation.

selfcheck.prompt: How do the three numbers change if you copy after the correction? Explain what state is preserved.
selfcheck.feedback: The output becomes 14 335 335. The objects are separate, but the snapshot was taken after the current reading changed.

practice.title: Calibration log
practice.task: Use the first line, up to 63 bytes. It contains three whitespace-separated integers. Later lines are ignored. The sensor ID is 1–9999, the original reading is 0–2000 mV, and the correction is -200–200 mV. Create one record, preserve a snapshot, add the correction and check that the result is in 0–2000. Print the ID, new reading and original reading separated by spaces. Print invalid for malformed input or an out-of-range result.
criteria: Values outside 0–2000 are rejected. Preserve the snapshot and output member order.
practice.hint: Compute adjusted using active.reading and value[2]. The starter already checks adjusted. Read the last output value from original.reading.

steps.action: Locate the snapshot in the starter and write both values down before the update.
steps.why: A prediction separates a formula error from an ordering error.
steps.expected: The snapshot contains 780 in the main case.

steps.action: Change the expression for adjusted and run an ordinary and a boundary case.
steps.why: The correction can be in range while the result is out of range.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: Give valid input with a negative correction and a result of exactly 0. Check that the snapshot differs from the result.

teaching.scene: A sensor log must keep the original measurement and show the corrected reading next to it. Use the three output fields to verify the identifier, correction and retained snapshot.

predict.prompt: current holds identifier 14 and 320 mV. The program copies it to archived, then adds 15 only to current.millivolts. Which three numbers does it print?
predict.answer: It prints 14 335 320. Both fields are copied first. The increment changes just one field of current, so archived.millivolts still holds 320.

apply.prompt: Sensor 73 recorded 1960 mV. An operator tests two independent adjustments, +40 and +41. What does each run print, and what does the last number on success prove?
apply.answer: The +40 adjustment reaches exactly 2000, so it prints 73 2000 1960. The last number comes from the snapshot taken before the correction. The +41 result is 2001, so the program prints invalid.

practice.strategy: Write down field names and original values, then calculate the proposed reading separately. Test the allowed boundary and the first value beyond it. For a success, check the identifier, current reading and snapshot separately.
practice.diagnosis: If both output readings are corrected, mark when the snapshot field was filled. What was the working reading by that point?

syntax.form:
struct Sample archived = current;
current.millivolts += correction;
syntax.explanation: Assignment between structures of the same type copies their member values. The int members in this example are separate integer copies.
syntax.mistake: A snapshot taken after the correction already contains the new value. Take the copy before changing the reading.
